title: Nostromo KV stripe and eviction playbook for onboarding
content:
Context:
This is a working playbook for onboarding the Nostromo family (nostromo-6B / nostromo-13B variants) into hosted + dedicated fleets. Primary risk observed in pre-prod: heavy KV stripe churn and localized hot shards causing eviction storms on a subset of GPU pods in us-west1 and eu-west3. This doc captures measurements, mitigation knobs, rollout gating, and an action plan for Q1 onboarding.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Nostromo sessions show ~6–9x higher average KV inserts per session vs baseline (redwood-base-7B) due to longer contexts + multi-turn assistant usage patterns.
- Without targeted mitigations, peak onboarding can produce transient eviction spikes that reduce per-GPU effective capacity by 18–30% in impacted zones.
- Recommended approach: staged striped prewarm + adaptive eviction tuning + region-priority routing. Rollout over 4 weeks with hard gating on KV miss/evict rate and tail latency.

Key observed metrics (pre-prod synthetic workload):
- avg tokens per session: 420 (peak 1,800)
- avg KV entries written per session: 5,200 (baseline 700)
- avg KV entry size: 192 bytes (mostly compressed key+value)
- per-request KV delta (new keys): 28 keys per request on average during initial context seeding
- observed per-GPU KV memory pressure increase: ~9.2 GiB per 1k concurrent sessions at 8K context capacity
- eviction churn metric (evicts/sec per pod): baseline 12 -> nostromo spike 220
- tail p95 generation latency delta during evict storms: +120–320 ms

Implication for fleet capacity planning:
- Effective slot reduction: assume conservative 20% headroom loss in pods that see frenetic stripe contention. For a region with 500 slots, plan for 100 slot-equivalent buffer during onboarding peak.
- Cross-region absorption: eu-west3 is projected to exceed comfortable headroom sooner; recommend traffic shaping to us-central and us-west1 for first 2 weeks.

Root cause hypothesis (summary):
1) Nostromo's dialogue format uses richer document-level keys and frequent partial updates which increase KV write amplification.
2) Hashing distribution skew for certain user IDs + sticky routing created concentrated hot stripes on a subset of KV shards.
3) Default eviction thresholds tuned for steady-state LRU add to cascade evictions when multiple hot sessions churn the same stripe.

Mitigation knobs (ordered by non-invasiveness):
- Client-side: advise model team to reduce per-turn metadata keys where safe (quick PR checklist in linked Confluence).
- Routing: enable per-customer KV-affinity spreading (soft-affinity) to avoid strict stickiness for first 72h of heavy traffic.
- Caching layer: enable interleaved stripe placement for nostromo sessions (stripe_count=8 recommended) to reduce single-shard pressure.
- Eviction policy: switch from strict LRU to two-tier LRU+freq (LFU dampening) for 48h windows during rollout; raises memory slightly but reduces churn.
- Prewarm: seed top-k prefixes from production prompt corpora into KV cache during shadowing. Use sampling to limit seed size.
- Admission: soft-limit client concurrency and degrade non-critical background tasks during onboarding windows.

Simulation snapshots (from local tooling run: kv-sim v0.9, seed=20260105):
Scenario A (no mitigation):
- concurrent sessions: 12k, region us-west1 impacted 60%
- avg evicts/sec/pod: 210
- effective throughput loss: 24%
Scenario B (stripe_count=8 + LFU dampen):
- concurrent sessions: 12k
- avg evicts/sec/pod: 34
- effective throughput loss: 5%
Scenario C (B + prewarm top-200 prompts):
- evicts/sec/pod: 12
- tail latency delta: +20ms

Rollout plan (4-week phased):
- Week 0 (pre-rollout prep, 5 days):
  - Add nostromo model to routing catalog as beta; prepare routing rule sets; schedule KV prewarm jobs; update runbooks.
  - Tests: end-to-end shadow traffic at 5% of expected production QPS.
- Week 1 (shadow + monitoring gating, 7 days):
  - Shadow at 10% to production with stripe placement enabled and LFU dampen on.
  - Gate: evicts/sec/pod < 40 and p95 latency <= baseline + 50ms for 48h before progressing.
- Week 2 (canary can accept small % traffic, 7 days):
  - Canary at 1% traffic in two regions (us-west1, us-east1). Monitor KV churn and CPU.
  - If gate fails, rollback to stripe_count=4 + increased prewarm.
- Week 3 (regional ramp, 7 days):
  - Ramp to 10–20% in low-risk regions (us-central, us-west1). Enable admission controls in eu-west3 to limit initial acceptance.
- Week 4 (global gradual ramp and optimization):
  - Full rollout conditional on 7-day stability: sustained evicts/sec/pod < 35 and cost delta within forecast.

Gating metrics (must be instrumented before starting):
- KV evictions/sec/pod (primary)
- KV miss rate
- KV write amplification (writes per session)
- p95 generation latency
- OOM or pod restarts
- per-region slot utilization and spare headroom

Operational runbook (if evict storm detected):
1) Throttle nostromo traffic at ingress rate limiter for affected region (cut by 30%).
2) Temporarily enable aggressive prewarm for top-1k prefixes (30 min window).
3) Increase stripe_count by 2 for affected model variants.
4) If p95 > baseline + 200ms after 10 min, shift traffic to fallback variant (nostromo-lite) and open incident.

Cost/benefit notes:
- LFU dampening increases resident KV by ~7% which increases RAM cost on GPUs, but reduces evict churn and downstream RPCs; net per-token cost reduces in simulations.
- Prewarm jobs incur transient IO and storage IOPS costs; budgeted at ~$1.2K per major prewarm run per region.

Open questions / decisions needed from model/product team:
- Can the model team provide a reduced metadata schema or an opt-in compact mode for first 90 tokens? (Action: @Meera to sync on 2026-01-13)
- Is there an acceptable fallback model variant (nostromo-lite) for degraded quality during severe capacity pressure?

Immediate action items (owner -> due):
- Instrument evicts/sec/pod dashboards and set alerts (Santiago Ruiz -> 2026-01-12).
- Run kv-sim with live QPS traces from prod week of 2026-01-05 and upload results (Devon Brooks -> 2026-01-15).
- Confluence checklist for nostromo onboarding to include client SDK key-size limits (Meera Patel -> 2026-01-14).
- Prepare routing rule playbook for priority shift to us-central (Ellen Cho -> 2026-01-18).

Notes / log (live edits):
- 2026-01-10: initial doc created after first shadow run.
- 2026-01-16: adjusted stripe recommendation from 4 -> 8 after follow-up sim showed hotspot reduction.
- 2026-01-29: added LFU dampening as an option after SRE requested lower churn approach.

Appendix: quick calculation example (for capacity planner)
- If avg KV per session = 5200 entries, entry size 192 bytes -> ~0.96 MiB/session resident.
- For target 10k concurrent sessions in a region -> ~9.6 GiB total additional resident KV.
- If pod has 40 GiB available for KV across n slots, this corresponds to ~23% of a single pod's KV budget; spread across 5 pods, impact drops to ~4.6% each.

References: linked_artifacts above; see Confluence "Nostromo-model-onboarding" for raw sim logs and raw payload samples.

End (draft).
